Posts speak negatively of Thermondo and Enpal, but they are opinions from two commenters, and the claim is a first-person decision.

Posters give real figures (JAZ 4.55, 4,500 kWh vs 18,000 kWh gas) and report good results.
One post uses LWWP alongside a running-cost comparison, but it doesn't show people generally use the abbreviation for this.

One post asserts old buildings with heat pumps are cold and expensive, and another says a wrong choice can be costly; neither is a general statement that they don't work well.
Several posters describe older houses with oil or gas heating and are planning a switch to a heat pump.
One poster says they keep reading it's hard to find a reputable energy consultant who knows the subject, but doesn't say they couldn't find one, and it's a single post.
EV-0056 wants pre-filled forms as a purchase argument, implying wanting paperwork relief, but doesn't say it's a burden; other posts are irrelevant.

The post says many call heat pumps Stromfresser and then argues against it with the 1 kW to 4 kW heat ratio.
Posts show cold-weather efficiency problems (electric backup below 4°C, idle in winter), but don't explicitly frame cold as the test of comfort and efficiency.
EV-0016 says finding a serious, knowledgeable consultant is difficult and EV-0017 hints at few craftspeople, but availability is only implied; EV-0018 is about prices.

One post advises limiting Vorlauftemperatur to 55 degrees to test; evidence doesn't show it's a go-to tip generally.

The post says to try limiting temperature and see, ending with 'Versuch macht klug'.
Posts show a banker and installer/consultant uncertain or giving differing views on residency, but not that 'nobody serves it' or that it's a common question.
EV-0015 shows asking about the KfW process, but the snippet doesn't mention paying a lot upfront.
One post is titled 'Wärmepumpe nach 1 Jahr', but it's a single example, not evidence of people generally.
Posts say comparison with others is unhelpful because houses and residents differ, but don't show owners want a reliable benchmark or that nobody offers one.
One post addresses someone as 'Forumsfreund' and asks about tariff/costs, and another references 'Forumsfreunden', but 'compare in detail' is only loosely shown.

Posts call the 50 ct/kWh tariff outrageously expensive and a problem for heat pump costs, but personal worry is not explicitly stated.
One post wants PV installed by year end for guaranteed funding; another plans to start heat pump work at year end with KfW funding context.
EV-0041 states heating load is worst-case, not average.
